permutationLabel: Early NSTI, LRINEC 0, minimal skin signs
summary: 38-year-old woman, 18 h after a cat scratch to the forearm: severe pain out of proportion, woody induration beyond faint erythema, HR 112, T 38.2 °C; WBC 13, CRP 90, normal Na, creatinine, glucose, Hb 13.9 (LRINEC 0).

inputs.hpi: Scratched by a cat on the right forearm yesterday. Overnight developed severe pain in the forearm, out of proportion to the faint redness, needing repeated morphine in the department. Feels feverish and unwell. Previously fit and well. Pregnancy test negative.

exam.general: Distressed by pain. HR 112, BP 118/72, T 38.2°C, RR 20.
exam.msk: Right forearm: faint pink erythema 4 × 6 cm around two scratches, woody hard induration of the forearm extending well beyond the erythema, severe tenderness beyond the skin changes, pain on passive finger extension. No crepitus. No bullae.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Necrotising fasciitis (suspected)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected early necrotising soft-tissue infection of the right forearm despite LRINEC 0 — pain out of proportion with induration beyond erythema. Needs urgent surgical exploration.

mustNotMiss.note: A LRINEC of 0 must not remove NSTI from the list when the clinical picture fits.

mustInclude.note: Clinical suspicion → surgical exploration (finger test / incision), not observation.

mustExclude.note: A low LRINEC must not be presented as reassurance. The iOS LRINEC calculator is not driven by this harness; see the findings report.
The documented plan must not be an oral cellulitis regimen.

A PE or ACS antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to a haemorrhagic or non-thrombotic diagnosis. Reading the iOS source, DiagnosisRadiationEngine.radiate matches keywords by substring and would attach the ACS plan ("mi" inside "abdominal", "limb", "haemodynamically") or the PE plan ("pe" inside "suspected", "penetrating", "superficial") to this diagnosis — to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: WSES/SIS-E consensus conference — management of skin and soft-tissue infections
guideline.section: Necrotising soft-tissue infections: clinical diagnosis (pain out of proportion, rapid progression, systemic toxicity); LRINEC has limited sensitivity and must not be used to rule out NSTI; prompt surgical debridement; empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics including an agent with anti-toxin activity (clindamycin) for streptococcal/clostridial infection; Fournier's gangrene
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Coccolini F, Kluger Y, et al. WSES/SIS-E consensus conference: recommendations for the management of skin and soft-tissue infections. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:58.

guideline.name: NSTI diagnostic accuracy — systematic review and meta-analysis
guideline.section: LRINEC ≥6 has low sensitivity for NSTI; a low score does not exclude it; clinical suspicion should prompt surgical exploration
guideline.citation: Fernando SM, Tran A, Cheng W, et al. Necrotizing soft tissue infection: diagnostic accuracy of physical examination, imaging, and LRINEC score: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Ann Surg. 2019;269:58–65.

guideline.name: LRINEC score (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotising Fasciitis)
guideline.section: Score items and weights: CRP ≥150 mg/L (4); WBC 15–25 (1), >25 (2); Hb 11–13.5 (1), <11 (2); Na <135 (2); creatinine >141 µmol/L (2); glucose >10 mmol/L (1)
guideline.citation: Wong CH, Khin LW, Heng KS, Tan KC, Low CO. The LRINEC (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis) score: a tool for distinguishing necrotizing fasciitis from other soft tissue infections. Crit Care Med. 2004;32:1535–41.

guideline.name: IDSA practice guideline — diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections (2014 update)
guideline.section: Purulent SSTI (abscess): incision and drainage; antibiotics active against MRSA when SIRS, immunocompromise or failed drainage; culture of abscess material. Non-purulent cellulitis: agent active against streptococci; severe: IV antibiotics and assess for necrotising infection. Necrotising infections: prompt surgical consultation, vancomycin plus piperacillin-tazobactam (or carbapenem), clindamycin for toxin suppression in streptococcal NF
guideline.citation: Stevens DL, Bisno AL, Chambers HF, et al. Practice guidelines for the diagnosis and management of skin and soft tissue infections: 2014 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America. Clin Infect Dis. 2014;59:e10–52.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Septic shock / high likelihood of sepsis: blood cultures before antimicrobials, antimicrobials within 1 h, lactate, source control as soon as practical
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: the same diagnosis with LRINEC 0. WSES/SIS and the Fernando meta-analysis: LRINEC has low sensitivity and must not rule out NSTI. The engines must keep NSTI on the differential, escalate, and plan surgical exploration. Tests whether a low score or near-normal labs lead to false reassurance.
